newsitem.title: UK: LME copper consolidates under $2,600, others soft.
newsitem.headline: LME copper consolidates under $2,600, others soft.

text.p: LME copper bounced modestly in the morning after stocks data showed a fall of 1,675 tonnes, but may not have enough momentum to revisit Thursday's highs above $2,600 per tonne, traders said.
Other metals were weaker, but largely within recent ranges.
Three month copper dipped nearly $10 from Thursday's afternoon kerb close of $2,580, but recovered to unchanged levels when the inventory data was released.
"There's not been a lot of activity so far, not too much volume," a trader said.
News that metals supply has been hit at Russia's Norilsk Nickel due to gas supply problems had no immediate impact on prices.
A spokesman said it was too early to say how much output was being lost at Norilsk, which also produces copper.
The market remained fundamentally tight, with the Inco strike removing about 9,000 tonnes of copper production from the market each month it continues, Flemings Global Mining Group said.
In Korea, LG Metals said the market had no need to worry about its current open metals options positions, declining to comment on rumours that it was facing huge losses.

Traders in London said copper's rally to a 13-month peak of $2,609 on Thurdsay was fuelled by options covering, and some players attributed a sudden slide in futures to an out-of-ring deal between LG Metals and a major U.S. investment bank.
An LG Metals spokesman said the firm had been conducting futures and options operations to hedge the risks arising from its physical base metal trades but declined to give details.
Other metals showed little incentive to move out of recent ranges.
Aluminium held at weaker levels after drifting lower in late inter-office trade on Thursday evening, ignoring a stocks fall of 3,775 tonnes.
It was last at $1,606, down from a kerb close of $1,615, with producer selling restraining any attempt to move higher.
"Producer selling is continuing to be seen on rallies, which suggests that some capacity restarts will be seen in the near future," broker GNI said.
"However, judging by the strength of demand at the moment, these will not be enough to balance the market," GNI added.
If support fails at the 10-day moving average of $1,604, prices could slip to the June 3 low of $1,575, chartists said.
Nickel was $55 weaker at $7,140 and a move this week below the 10-day moving average was not positive for prices, analysts said.
Zinc lost $4 to $1,355 after stocks rose by 3,275 tonnes and lead was indicated at $627/$630, down from $635.
Tin was little changed at $5,600/20 versus $5,610 while alloy was at $1,480/85 after $1,483/87.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
